- If sentiment is positive (≥0.10) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.20), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +30%+ in 3-5 days); cap forecast at 10-15% above recent peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3-5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to reverse; add 5-10% upward bias to counteract.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates in early period (first 5-7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; add 2-5% upward adjustment.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.28, -0.28), model tends to ignore them; increase forecast by 3-5% to account for sentiment-driven volatility.
